The findings suggest early Mars had a dynamic hydrosphere and a more complex mantle evolution than previously thought, pointing to potentially habitable environments in its crust.

The findings demonstrate that evolution has independently converged on similar decision-making mechanisms in birds and mammals, offering insights into how different brain architectures process visual information efficiently.

Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access

Global · Useful · Updated

Briefing produced 26 Oct 2026, 10:57 PM NZDT

Security researcher Sammy Hajhamid demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Nintendo Switch 2, achieving userland access to run homebrew and modify games. The exploit leverages a 32-bit integer overflow in SmileBasic 4 and a buffer overflow in the FileSystem services module to gain privileged filesystem actions and native code execution. The hack is tethered, requiring a macOS or Linux PC on the same network, and currently operates within a sandbox that lacks full kernel-level control.

Why it matters

Nintendo has delisted SmileBasic 4 from the eShop to limit exploit spread, but the vulnerability is expected to be patched in imminent firmware updates, which are required for continued access to Nintendo services and future game releases.

The political ad wars are still being fought over the airwaves even as digital gains share

United States · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 26 Oct 2026, 10:57 PM NZDT

Broadcast television is forecast to capture 48% of the $11.6 billion in political advertising spend for the 2025-26 US midterm elections, according to AdImpact. This share is significantly higher than broadcast's 7.7% of total general advertising spend, driven by the medium's perceived trust and reach in local counties. Publicly traded broadcasters like Nexstar and Gray Media reported high political ad revenues in their recent quarters.

Why it matters

Political advertising provides high-margin revenue for broadcasters, helping them manage debt.

David's Bridal plans to spin off AI platform Pearl into publicly traded company

Global · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 26 Oct 2026, 10:57 PM NZDT

David's Bridal filed a nonbinding letter of intent to spin off its AI platform, Pearl, into a standalone public company targeting a $350 million valuation, with the deal expected to close in the first half of 2027. Pearl will own the company's intellectual property and license it back to David's Bridal, while projecting over 100% revenue growth in 2027 and an EBITDA margin exceeding 30% this year.

Why it matters

The spinoff aims to leverage Pearl's positive cash flow and existing customer base to attract talent and fuel growth, distinct from the struggling AI stock market, while allowing David's Bridal to focus on its physical retail operations.
